newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday February 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday February 11.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* In a letter to a newspaper, opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi says he agrees to bring forward the 1998 budget and to discuss in parliament the need for public spending cuts but warns PDS leader Massimo D'Alema : "He must say if he stands with us and (Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio) Ciampi or with (hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader) Bertinotti." (Il Messaggero).
* The Treasury Ministry is reportedly examining a plan in two stages to reform retirement pensions by the year 2000-2002 (Corriere della Sera).

* Fausto Bertinotti in an interview threatens harsh political confrontation and trade unions leader Sergio Cofferati reaffirms his opposition to any discussion about pensions before 1998 (La Repubblica).
* Italy's highest court ruled that a military court should hear the war crimes retrial of former SS captain Erich Priebke (all).
* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said markets are reacting well after the G7 weekend meeting in Berlin and inflation is falling at world level (all).
* Transport minister Claudio Burlando is expected to meet today railway unions' representatives who are protesting against cost cutting measures included in the 1997 budget (all).
* Italian new car registrations rose 4.38 percent to 207,000 units in January, compared with 198,308 in January 1996 (all).

* Negotiations are reportedly underway between state telecom holding Stet, US telephone company GTE and Teleglobe International of Canada to set up an alliance "in a very short time" (Il Sole 24 ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
